components.export_notes: BUILT 2026-09-30 (this cycle) -- this checkpoint is SAC (algorithm mislabeled in its own filename prefix ppo_goal_cw_*, verified via zip contents: actor/critic/ent_coef optimizer state), the FIRST SAC checkpoint export attempted anywhere in this project; export_policy_np.py/np_policy.py had no SAC actor path at all (only PPO MlpPolicy/GRU/dual-GRU/transformer). Added `_sac_mlp_payload` (SAC's deterministic actor tanh(mu(latent_pi(obs))), verified numerically ~6e-8 max diff vs SB3 for random obs -- this project's SAC action spaces are exactly Box(-1,1) so tanh IS the actor's own squash, no extra scale/bias) reusing the existing generic N-layer `layers` format with a new additive `meta.output_squash` field ("clip" default = unchanged prior behavior, "tanh" = new). Also added `relu` to the nlayer activation set (SAC's own latent_pi activation) and an explicit `meta.walk_yaw_offset_cmd`/`walk_yaw_offset_set` contract disambiguating obs-width-74's TWO colliding families (the pre-existing phase-clock family, which needs phase_hz, vs this checkpoint's static per-episode [target,error] yaw-offset pair, which has no clock at all -- forcing a fabricated phase_hz onto it would have been actively wrong metadata). export_policy_np.py --training-hz 50 --inner-hz 50 --extra-meta '{"walk_yaw_offset_cmd":true,"walk_yaw_offset_set":[15,30,45,90,-15,-30,-45,-90]}', net-arch 256,256,128, parity 4.66e-06 over 200 random obs (bar 1e-5). All new mechanics covered by new tests in test_np_policy.py/test_export_policy_np.py (full suite green except two pre-existing unrelated flakes -- test_dual_gru_numpy_sequence_matches_torch_and_threads_both_cores float-tolerance flake and test_course_disp_semantics.py::test_real_failed_checkpoint_ema_inert_disp_active, both reproduce identically on the pre-change tree). NOTE: this export is weights-only parity evidence -- the robot-side linux_control runtime has no consumer for a walk_yaw_offset_cmd observation yet (no joystick-driven relative-heading-offset command source exists in linux_control/ today); that plumbing is separate, larger, not-yet-scoped Robot-Lab-side work and is NOT claimed done here.

composition_mechanism.type: segment-alternating role composition, two env instances, cross-env physical-state reanchor at each boundary
composition_mechanism.description: Two SimHexapodJointWalkEnv instances (one per role's own versioned cfg-set recipe -- cfg_recipe_walk50hz_rlonly_v2 / cfg_recipe_walkyaw50hz_acq5_seedsweep, whose SimServoParams/_act_to_q caches differ: box_yaw 15 vs 30deg, term_penalty 24 vs 400, safety.max_roll/pitch 30 vs 45 -- so they cannot hot-swap mid-episode on one live env, exactly eval_lifecycle_handoff_rlonly.py's own precedent). At each segment boundary the raw physical state (qpos/qvel/ctrl/act + safety slew memory) is copied across via the SAME capture_physical_state/apply_physical_state helpers, optionally through --settle-grounded-s (opt-in, waits for a fully-grounded tick before reanchor; default off, bit-exact prior behavior -- built 2026-09-30, does not change this candidate's own numbers, see caveats below). No scripted joint trajectory, teacher target, or demonstration enters the composition at any point.
composition_mechanism.curve_speed_flag: --curve-speed feeds the FROZEN turn-and-hold checkpoint a nonzero body-frame vx SIMULTANEOUSLY with its yaw-offset target during the turn segment -- a command combination absent from its own training (every yaw-offset training episode hard-zeros vx/vy). This is zero-shot OOD generalization of an existing checkpoint, not a new policy. --curve-speed 0.0 recovers the original stationary stop-turn-go schedule (the 'bundle_rlonly_stopturngo_v1' framing named in walkcurr/STATUS.md 2026-09-30 before the curved-walking read superseded it same-cycle) -- both command profiles are the SAME two checkpoints and the SAME tool, differing only in this one eval-time flag, so this single manifest covers both.
